title: Culling Lights in Mobile is broken
body:
### Tested versions

reproduced on 4.3 stable, 4.4 beta 2

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta2 - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Single-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6600 (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.12033.1030) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-10105F CPU @ 3.70GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

First image is expected result, the final light is half broken as one half is on a mesh that has only that light, the other half is on the mesh that already has 8 lights affecting it and thus isn't rendered per the mobile renderer limit of 8 lights per mesh

No OC
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e258e03d-02ed-422b-8285-53152406da77)

OC
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7331c89-29cf-461c-8663-e1097b156949)

Occluded Light Hidden
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/925142e9-50ca-4bbf-b0d0-2e2e3be6f811)

FC Video (Ignore the apparent 9 lights at the end, the light that got toggled back on is also partially clipped it's just the setup of strips that gives the illusion of the limit being broken here

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88b830dc-4f5a-42af-a370-658da4abf707


### Steps to reproduce

Hide the occluder and toggle the TOGGLE spotlight on and off to get only half the light
Activate the Occluder and occlude some of the 8 lights in a row -> no change for the half light
Manually hide a light from the row -> half light turns to full light as the other half of the strip is no longer affected by 8 lights

Alternatively, you can attempt to frustum cull the 8 lights in a row and it will also fail to fix the "broken" light

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mobile.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18614366/mobile.zip)
